alt_titles: HYPER-IgE SYNDROME WITH ATYPICAL MYCOBACTERIOSIS, AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that immunodeficiency-35 (IMD35), also known as tyrosine kinase-2 (TYK2) deficiency, is caused by homozygous mutation in the TYK2 gene.

paragraphs.text: Immunodeficiency-35 (IMD35) is an autosomal recessive primary immunodeficiency caused by TYK2 deficiency. Patients are susceptible to intracellular bacteria, such as mycobacteria (including BCG and Mycobacterium tuberculosis), Salmonella and Brucella, and/or to viral infections, mainly herpesviruses. Kreins et al. (2015) attributed these infections to impaired responses to IL-12 and IFN-alpha/beta. The first patient reported had features of hyper-IgE syndrome (HIES), including atopic dermatitis, high serum IgE, and staphylococcal infections (Minegishi et al., 2006). Most later patients had none of these features, and Kreins et al. (2015) concluded that HIES is not an intrinsic part of TYK2 deficiency.

paragraphs.text: Minegishi et al. (2006) reported a patient who had been clinically diagnosed with hyper-IgE syndrome. He had unusual susceptibility to various microorganisms, including viruses, fungi and mycobacteria, and had atopic dermatitis with elevated serum IgE. Kreins et al. (2015) gave more detail on this patient (P1), a Japanese man born to consanguineous parents. He had atopic dermatitis from age 1 month and recurrent bacterial and viral infections from age 1 year. He developed BCGitis at age 22 months, 6 months after vaccination. He had repeated Staphylococcus aureus skin abscesses, pneumonia without pneumatoceles, otitis and sinusitis. At age 15 years he had sepsis after severe nontyphi Salmonella enterocolitis. His viral infections included parainfluenza virus-3 pneumonia, recurrent oral HSV infections and molluscum contagiosum, and he had mild oral candidiasis. Tests repeatedly showed hypereosinophilia (701-800/microliter) and high serum IgE (1,430-2,100 IU/ml). At age 30 years he had ocular sarcoidosis.

paragraphs.text: Kilic et al. (2012) reported a Turkish boy, born in 1992 to healthy first-cousin parents, who had TYK2 deficiency without HIES. He received BCG vaccine at 2 months of age. Left axillary lymphadenopathy appeared at 8 months, and generalized lymphadenopathy at 21 months. He had fistulous cervical, axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy, and M. bovis BCG was isolated from the draining cervical sinuses. The PPD skin test was negative. At 8 years of age he developed neurobrucellosis, with Brucella spp. grown from blood and cerebrospinal fluid, after eating unpasteurized cheese. The illness left him with severe cognitive impairment and severe hearing loss, and MRI showed lacunar infarcts. At 11 years he had herpes zoster of the right maxillary branch of the trigeminal nerve. He had no skeletal or dental features of HIES and no atopy, asthma, candidiasis, boils or cold abscesses. Serum IgE measured at ages 2, 11, 16 and 18 years was normal or slightly high (80, 115, 218 and 155 IU/ml).

paragraphs.text: Kreins et al. (2015) reported 7 TYK2-deficient patients from 5 unrelated families, all with consanguineous parents. The patients came from Turkey, Morocco, Iran and Argentina. P2 was the Turkish patient reported by Kilic et al. (2012). P3, a Moroccan girl, had disseminated extrapulmonary tuberculosis from age 13 years and died of it. Her younger brother (P4) had meningitis of unknown cause at 8 months of age, recurrent otitis and urinary tract infections, asthma, and eczema of the ear canal. P5, an Iranian boy, had BCG lymphadenitis and later paravertebral and psoas abscesses with fistulization and pulmonary involvement. His younger sister (P6) had BCG lymphadenopathy and an unknown viral skin infection. P7, a 9-year-old Iranian girl, had M. tuberculosis disease with micronodular lung infiltrates and adenopathies. P8, an 11-year-old boy from Argentina, had recurrent herpes gingivostomatitis, aseptic herpes meningitis, disseminated cutaneous herpetic lesions and mild mental disability. None of the 7 had atopy, high serum IgE, staphylococcal or other pyogenic infections, or fungal infections. Infections with weakly virulent intracellular bacteria responded to antibiotics and did not recur.

paragraphs.text: Wu et al. (2020) reported a Chinese boy born to nonconsanguineous parents. After BCG vaccination on the third day of life he had recurrent abscess and ulceration at the injection site. At 14 months of age he developed BCG lymphadenitis of the left axillary nodes. From 6 months of age he had recurrent respiratory tract infections and diarrhea. Pathogens identified included Salmonella, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, M. bovis BCG and influenza viruses. He had no high serum IgE, atopy, staphylococcal illness or lymphopenia. He had a small head circumference and began to say simple words at 3 years and 4 months. In a review of 12 reported patients, Wu et al. (2020) found intracellular bacterial infections in 7 (58%) and recurrent viral infections in 7 (58%). None had the facial features, bone abnormalities, delayed shedding of primary teeth or aneurysms seen in STAT3-related HIES.

paragraphs.text: Zhang et al. (2022) studied an international cohort of 112 children hospitalized for COVID-19 pneumonia. Three unrelated Turkish children with TYK2 deficiency were found, aged 2, 4 and 9 years and each born to consanguineous parents. The 2-year-old girl had moderate COVID-19 pneumonia; earlier she had been hospitalized for infection with VZV vaccine and diagnosed with Kawasaki disease at 11 months. The 2 boys had critical COVID-19 pneumonia needing high-flow oxygen in intensive care. The 4-year-old boy had been in intensive care for influenza pneumonia at 3 years of age. His 3-year-old sister had the same genotype; she had critical influenza pneumonia needing intubation and disseminated varicella, but had not been infected with SARS-CoV-2.

agent.process_note: I read the full texts of Kilic 2012 and Wu 2020 in full. I read the full text of Kreins 2015 through the Results, Discussion and Case reports sections. For Zhang 2022 I read the abstract and the passages about TYK2. Minegishi 2006, Fuchs 2016 and Lv 2022 were available only as abstracts, and Woellner 2007 only as a title, so Woellner 2007 is not cited. I searched for consanguinity, variant names, IL-6 findings and segregation. The papers disagree on the numbering of the Turkish patient's 9-bp deletion: Kilic gives c.2302_2310del and Kreins gives c.2303_2311del. Minegishi's original mutation is not named in its abstract; Kreins describes it as a 4-bp deletion in exon 4 (C70HfsX21), and Wu's table lists it as c.550_553delGCTT. The Fuchs abstract does not name the mutation; the c.647delC (P216RfsX14) assignment comes only from Wu's review table. Zhang calls the same frameshift a 'missense' variant in one sentence. I could not find the mutations of Lv 2022 in its abstract. No HGNC reference data were supplied, so the TYK2 MIM number and chromosomal location are left out.
